import pandas as pd
import ast

# Source file paths
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/training_1.csv"

# Step 1: Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Step 2: Inspect schemas
# Source0 columns: ['userId', 'movieId', 'rating', 'timestamp']
# Source1 columns: ['movieId', 'title', 'genres']

# Step 3: Join Source0 and Source1 on 'movieId' (common key)
df_merged = pd.merge(df_source0, df_source1, on='movieId', how='inner')

# Step 4: Create 'genres_arr' column by splitting 'genres' string on '|'
df_merged['genres_arr'] = df_merged['genres'].apply(lambda x: str(x).split('|') if pd.notnull(x) else [])

# Step 5: Create 'genre_count' column as the first genre in the genres list (string)
# According to target examples, genre_count is a string and equals the first genre in genres_arr
df_merged['genre_count'] = df_merged['genres_arr'].apply(lambda arr: arr[0] if len(arr) > 0 else '')

# Step 6: Ensure data types match target schema:
# 'userId': integer
df_merged['userId'] = df_merged['userId'].astype(int)
# 'movieId': integer
df_merged['movieId'] = df_merged['movieId'].astype(int)
# 'rating': float
df_merged['rating'] = df_merged['rating'].astype(float)
# 'timestamp': integer
df_merged['timestamp'] = df_merged['timestamp'].astype(int)
# 'title': string (already string)
df_merged['title'] = df_merged['title'].astype(str)
# 'genres': string (already string)
df_merged['genres'] = df_merged['genres'].astype(str)
# 'genres_arr': string representation of list
df_merged['genres_arr'] = df_merged['genres_arr'].apply(lambda arr: str(arr))
# 'genre_count': string (already string)

# Step 7: Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
target_columns = ['userId', 'movieId', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'title', 'genres', 'genres_arr', 'genre_count']
df_target = df_merged[target_columns]

# Step 8: Write the result to the target CSV file without the index column
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join on movieId
df = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movieId", how="inner")

# Create genres_arr by splitting genres string on '|'
df["genres_arr"] = df["genres"].str.split("|")

# Create genre_count as the first genre (leftmost genre)
df["genre_count"] = df["genres_arr"].apply(lambda x: x[0] if isinstance(x, list) and len(x) > 0 else "")

# Reorder columns to match target schema
df = df[["userId", "movieId", "rating", "timestamp", "title", "genres", "genres_arr", "genre_count"]]

# Write output
df.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_15/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
